note: Research method: WebSearch only (WebFetch/curl blocked). Quotes are taken from search-engine excerpts of the cited page (mostly sozai.app transcript summaries of JJ's own videos, his own sales pages, and third-party write-ups). facts.claim: Expected value framing for funded accounts: probability of payout × payout size; buy accounts only if expected payouts exceed expenses.
facts.quote: Expected value helps estimate profitability by multiplying the probability of payout by the payout size. It allows traders to assess if their payouts will exceed expenses before buying accounts. On funded accounts, the only goal is to maximize expected value.

facts.claim: Different objective per account type: optimize pass rate on evals, maximize EV on funded.

facts.claim: Eval phase: maximum risk, clear the whole target in exactly two trades of roughly half the target each (satisfies ~50% consistency rules), then move on; a lost eval is 'cheap'.

contradictions: Account count: 20–30 (his X posts) vs 40 (video attribution) vs 45+ (Chart Fanatics blurb). Likely grew over time; no per-firm breakdown found anywhere.

Execution: he says the optimal way is one account at a time, one trade per account per day, and not to copy trade until ~$20k/month; yet third-party summaries (fttuts, TikTok) describe copying one trade across dozens of accounts, and jjwebinar says he 'cycles one trade across multiple funded accounts'. Probably: evals traded individually, funded accounts copied.

Trades per day: 'about 10 trades per day' (sozai $1.6M; his own 80 trades/8 days) vs '30 times/day' (Chart Fanatics title) vs 10–30 (task brief). 'One trade per account per day' × many accounts reconciles these.
Payout totals rise across sources ($1.2M→$2M+) and 'verified' is self-asserted; E8 certificate is the only firm-issued proof surfaced.
Stop sizes are quoted as 'ticks' in youtubesummary/one search summary but as 'points' (50/25/16.5) on fxreplay; points ($20/pt NQ) matches the ~$1,000 risk figure.
Tradeify is named on jjwebinar as a payout source but did not appear in the $1.6M per-firm breakdown excerpt.
